reminders.guidance: Embed the exact template the grader uses (byte-for-byte, hash-checked) in your training code and render one example both ways before launching.
reminders.symptom: Training and grading render different strings for the same conversation; the model is trained on one format and graded on another.

reminders.guidance: Keep the required full model, tokenizer and processor files with the selected artifact. Check local metadata on CPU, then perform any model-loading/evaluation probe under its prior matching locked card in the actual serving environment before the deadline. A CPU metadata check alone does not prove vLLM loadability. Preserve the measured on-disk generation settings through export; a serialization repair must not silently change the selected decoder.
reminders.symptom: The final evaluation scores the base model or fails to load; hours of training count for nothing.

reminders.guidance: Use the datasets version the harness ships (PostTrainBench container: datasets==4.5.0) and pin dataset revisions in setup.data[].source.
reminders.symptom: A dataset that downloaded fine elsewhere fails to load, or loads with a different schema.

reminders.guidance: Read save-safety.md and instrument supported native saves with GenerationSaveContract, using SaveSafeTrainer for intermediate and final Trainer saves. Check after in-code repairs before expensive work and again at the actual save boundary. Preserve selected serving JSON bytes separately. This is not a blanket parent-config or eval-only preflight blocker; unsupported paths remain explicitly unverified.
reminders.symptom: Training reaches a checkpoint or merge finishes accumulating weights, then strict generation-config serialization raises before a usable model is saved.

reminders.guidance: Never end the turn while training, sampling or evaluation is alive. Prefer one foreground script with a long Bash timeout that runs the producer, checks its exit status and artifacts, then evaluates. If backgrounding is necessary, capture the producer PID and use `wait "$pid"` in the same shell that launched it; a later Bash call cannot wait on another shell's child. Otherwise read the tool's task-completion result or poll the actual producer's process state at most 60 seconds apart, with an exit result retained by the launch wrapper or task handle. If it is unavailable, report unknown exit status rather than assuming a vanished PID succeeded. A launcher or leftover vLLM engine is not the producer. An unchanged tail, existing file or GPU memory alone proves neither life nor death: quiet runs may be alive and crashed runs leave stale artifacts. After exit check the reported status, current-run artifact identity/freshness and required contents before accepting results or starting a dependent stage; after failure record failed/killed instead of chaining blindly. Fill sections 5-6 and close the card. Detached launches may still use `setsid nohup <cmd> > <log> 2>&1 < /dev/null &`, but detachment is not a completion or success check. The Stop hook blocks session end while a locked card remains open.
reminders.symptom: The trace ends with "I'll report back when the run finishes"; the training log stops mid-epoch; final_model/ is never written; most of the budget is unused.

reminders.guidance: Render with the actual grader template, then pass token IDs or tokenize with add_special_tokens=False when the rendered string already contains special tokens. Resolve explicit stop_token_ids from that tokenizer/template, including n>1 routes; [1,106] was this historical Gemma route, not a universal constant. Preserve raw draws before scoring and handle non-finite numeric parses as explicit failed/invalid samples. Under a matching prior locked card, use a budgeted probe that records token IDs and engine finish/stop reasons; a literal EOT suffix is not a stop-reason measurement. Check the actual owned producer/engine process before relaunching; nvidia-smi alone establishes neither ownership nor completion. Estimate throughput from the actual probe.
reminders.symptom: A sampling pass keeps almost nothing (0.8 % correct; 86 % of samples running past the first answer; 0 % pass at n>1 while n=1 works); the first token ids of every prompt read [2, 2, ...]; the scorer dies after the whole pass with "OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer"; the relaunch after a kill fails with "Free memory 16/79 GiB".
